messages:
maya: Customer (Acme Retail) seeing intermittent 401s in Console when fetching model list. They gave a request id: req_0a9f3c. Happens in Chrome during a demo — can we send clear HAR + console + curl repro instructions?

alex: Got it. Can you confirm account id and exact time window? Also ask them not to paste tokens in-channel.

acme-customer: Account acct-9382. Window ~2026-03-16 15:12-15:20 UTC. We redacted tokens but the response header shows x-request-id=req_0a9f3c.

support-bot: deploy-bot: Finished deploy console-service@v2.1.4 at 2026-03-16T14:58:23Z (deploy-889) :information_source:

jordan: Thanks — common causes: expired/rotated tokens, clock skew, or a proxy dropping Authorization header. Best repro package: HAR + Console logs + a copied cURL of the failing request + server request id/time window.

maya: Pasting simple instructions to send to customer (Chrome & Firefox). Keep them short.

maya: === Chrome: capture HAR + console logs ===
1) Open Chrome, go to the page that hits the API (Console -> Models list).
2) Open DevTools (F12) -> Network tab -> check "Preserve log".
3) Reproduce the problem (refresh / click the models button).
4) Find the failing request (filter "models" or look for status 401). Click it -> Headers -> look for `x-request-id`.
5) Right-click the request in the Network list -> "Save all as HAR with content" -> attach file.
6) In DevTools -> Console tab -> right-click -> "Save as..." to export console logs (or copy visible lines).
7) Right-click the failing request -> "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL" and paste here (please redact your token or replace it with <REDACTED>).

maya: Example curl (please redact actual token before sharing):
```
curl 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -i
```

maya: Look for these headers in the request/response: Authorization, x-request-id, date, x-forwarded-for. If the Authorization header is missing in the captured request, tell them to check browser extensions/proxies.

maya: === Firefox quick steps ===
- DevTools -> Network -> check "Persist Logs" -> reproduce -> right-click any request -> "Save All As HAR". Console logs: Console panel -> right-click -> "Export Visible Messages".

jordan: If they can't share tokens: they can copy the cURL which will include the header; we only need the header name/value pattern. They should replace the token with `<REDACTED>` when uploading. Also include the exact timestamp range and the x-request-id (we have req_0a9f3c).

alex: For server-side correlation, we also need a debug bundle from their account if possible. Provide this CLI snippet (support-only):
```
rwd-support bundle --account acct-9382 --since "2026-03-16T15:00:00Z" --until "2026-03-16T15:30:00Z" --request-id req_0a9f3c > acme-debug-bundle.tar.gz
```

alex: If they cannot run CLI, they can trigger a debug bundle from Console -> Settings -> Support -> "Collect debug bundle" and paste the generated link here.

maya: Quick privacy note: please redact Authorization tokens and any PII before uploading. If they need secure upload, we can provide a signed S3 link (ask me). :lock:

acme-customer: Thanks, uploading HAR + console.txt and cURL now. I redacted the token and left x-request-id and timestamps.

jordan: Perfect. Once we have the HAR and curl we’ll check whether the Authorization header was sent and correlate req_0a9f3c in the logs. If header is present but backend returns 401, we’ll look at token validation and key rotation window.

maya: I'll confirm when files are attached. Thanks team. :pray:
